item.research_question: How does the Al concentration (3.5 to 54 at.%) influence phase formation and magnetic properties in FeMnCoCrAl high entropy alloy thin films?
item.material_system: FeMnCoCrAl high entropy alloy thin films with Al content varying from 3.5 to 54 at.%
item.processing_route: Co-sputtering of equiatomic FeMn, Co, Cr, and Al targets on Si (100) and Al2O3 (0001) substrates; power density varied from 2 to 7.5 W cm−2 for Al target; base pressure 2 × 10−5 Pa; Ar gas at 0.4 Pa; deposition time 22 min; substrate temperature <80 °C
item.test_conditions: Room temperature magnetic hysteresis (VSM, 5 T max field), temperature-dependent magnetization (10 mT field), XRD (grazing incidence, Co Kα), EDX, Atom Probe Tomography (60 K, 30 pJ laser pulse), TEM (200 kV), electrical resistivity (four-point probe, Van-der-Pauw method)
key_findings: Al additions to FeMnCoCr (α-Mn structure) induce formation of a body-centered cubic (BCC) phase, with a single BCC random solid solution forming at 8 at.% Al.
The largest saturation magnetization (Ms) of 82 Am2/kg was measured for the film containing 8 at.% Al.
Increasing Al concentration beyond 8 at.% causes a continuous decrease in Ms, dropping to 37 Am2/kg at 20 at.% Al and 7 Am2/kg at 40 at.% Al.
Thin films with Al concentrations of 26 at.% and 40 at.% exhibit nanoscale chemical separation (Al-Co rich regions) not resolved by standard XRD.
The 8 at.% Al single BCC phase thin film possesses a Curie temperature (Tc) greater than 900 K.
The coercivity (Hc) decreases from 13 mT at 4 at.% Al to 2.1 mT at 40 at.% Al, correlating with a reduction in column width from ~54 nm to ~20 nm.
The single phase BCC film containing 8 at.% Al exhibits an electrical resistivity of 151 µΩ cm, which increases with higher Al concentrations.
item.mechanism: Al additions stabilize the BCC phase over the FCC phase by forming a pseudogap at the Fermi level. The increase in Ms at low Al content is due to the formation of the ferromagnetic BCC phase, while the subsequent decrease is caused by the dilution of ferromagnetic species (Fe, Co) by paramagnetic Al and lattice distortions from Al's larger atomic radius. Nanoscale segregation in high-Al films further reduces magnetization by reducing ferromagnetic exchange interactions.
item.limitations: The thin film synthesis involves high quenching rates, so the composition boundaries for phase formation might deviate from those obtained by near-equilibrium processing. The study notes that more detailed investigations on factors affecting coercivity and magnetic anisotropy are subject of future work.
item.future_work: More detailed investigations on factors affecting Hc and the effects of magnetic anisotropy are subject of future work. The authors also suggest the material system may enable applications in magneto-caloric devices or high-frequency inductors.
quotes: Al additions to FeMnCoCr crystallizing in the alpha-Mn structure cause the formation of the body centered cubic (BCC) structure.
The largest saturation magnetization was measured for the film containing 8 at.% of Al.
The formation of a pseudogap at the Fermi level indicating the stabilization of the BCC phase over the FCC phase.
